messages.subject: Include Eigen::Tensor in TMB model template
messages.subject_clean: Include Eigen::Tensor in TMB model template
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I would like to include the `Eigen::Tensor` library in some TMB model code. I am getting compiler errors when I include the header, I believe due to namespace clashes with TMB.

If I include `TMB.hpp` before `Tensor`:
```
#include <TMB.hpp>
#include <unsupported/Eigen/CXX11/Tensor>
```

I get the following error:

```
      explicit specialization of non-template struct 'Rf_eval'
struct eval<Tensor<_Scalar, NumIndices_, Options, IndexType_>, Eigen::Dense>
       ^   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/include/Rinternals.h:1555:16: note: expanded from macro
      'eval'
#define eval                    Rf_eval
                                ^
```

If I include `Tensor` before `TMB`, I get the error:

```
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.0/Resources/library/TMB/include/tmbutils/density.hpp:106:3: error:
      reference to 'array' is ambiguous
  TYPEDEFS(scalartype_);
  ^
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.0/Resources/library/TMB/include/tmbutils/density.hpp:15:9: note:
      expanded from macro 'TYPEDEFS'
typedef array<scalartype> arraytype
        ^
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.0/Resources/library/TMB/include/tmbutils/array.hpp:22:8: note:
      candidate found by name lookup is 'tmbutils::array'
struct array:Map< Array<Type,Dynamic,1> >{
       ^
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.0/Resources/library/RcppEigen/include/unsupported/Eigen/CXX11/src/util/EmulateArray.h:229:38: note:
      candidate found by name lookup is 'Eigen::array'
template <typename T, std::size_t N> using array = std::array<T, N>;
```

Does anyone have experience with this? Is there a correct way to specify this or a workaround?

Below is example code and console output.

Many thanks,
Jeff

-----

```
library(TMB)
library(RcppEigen)

code1 <- '
#include <TMB.hpp>
#include <unsupported/Eigen/CXX11/Tensor>
//
template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
{
  PARAMETER(p);
  Type val(p*p);
  return val;
}
```

Hello,

Further to this -- I have managed a workaround, though not at all sure if it is a correct or optimal fix:

1. Explicitly reference tmbutils::array in the headers include/tmbutils/density.hpp and include/tmbutils/R_inla.hpp to avoid clash with Eigen::array when <Tensor> header is included.
The forked package with that patch is here: https://github.com/jeffeaton/adcomp/commits/tmbutils-array-namespace
The patch I applied is on this commit: https://github.com/jeffeaton/adcomp/commit/b156ab4004eaf1154d95241c66203705f7d315c8

2. Include the <Tensor> header before the <TMB.hpp> header. The other order throws an error, which I have not attempted to debug:

   >  unsupported/Eigen/CXX11/src/Tensor/TensorTraits.h:122:8: error:
   >    explicit specialization of non-template struct 'Rf_eval'

3. Add the compiler flag: -Wno-invalid-partial-specialization. Without this, threw an error: class template partial specialization is not more specialized than the primary template. This is apparently a known issue with a previous Eigen release, and maybe resolved by updating the Eigen headers included in TMB (not tried): https://github.com/owlbarn/eigen/issues/2#issuecomment-353763166

Here's a code snippet installing the patch version and confirming compiles model:

code2 <- '
#include <unsupported/Eigen/CXX11/Tensor>  // must include before <TMB.hpp>

#include <TMB.hpp>
//
template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
{
  PARAMETER(p);
  Type val(p*p);
  return val;
}
'

f2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".cpp")
writeLines(code2, f2)

TMB::compile(f2, flags = "-w -Wno-invalid-partial-specialization")

I'm interested to know if this breaks anything else or if there is a better recommended solution.

Many thanks,
Jeff

messages.subject: implementing splines with null-spaces in TMB
messages.subject_clean: implementing splines with null-spaces in TMB
messages.body_plain:
I've been playing around with fitting different spline effects using the GMRF function in the R_inla library in TMB.  I'm wondering if anyone has any thoughts on what to do if a penalty has a null-space.

My approach has generally been to construct the penalty matrix elsewhere (usually using mgcv but sometimes other packages) and then just sending this to the likelihood template.

If the penalty matrix has a null space then some of the columns are zero and GMRF()will throw an error.  There are various approaches to dealing with this, I have tried two of them and I am considering a third.  I'll summarise them:

"shrinkage smoother"  -  In mgcv you can choose the shrinkage smoother version of the thin plate penalty and cubic spline penalty.  This basically adds a small number to the null-space columns, I think by taking the smallest non-zero eigenvalue and dividing by some fixed number.  I have used this and it sometimes works will but in some models I get NaN errors, particularly in some models I've tried in higher dimensions where the null space is larger.  I've implemented my own version of this for some penalties that don't have shrinkage versions in mgcv (the GP Matern and Duchon splines).

"add another penalty matrix"  -  Mentioned in Simon Wood's GAM book but not implemented in mgcv I don't think.  Take eigendecomposition of the penalty matrix UDU^{-1}, then if Z are the cols of U that correspond to zero eigenvalues construct ZZ' as a new penalty matrix.  This comes at the expense of estimating an additional smoothing parameter.

This seems to work quite well - no more NaN errors anyway and seems less adhoc than the shrinkage smoother.  Models that I can't fit using the shrinkage approach I can fit using this and the results look okay.  I sometimes get a non-PD precision matrix at the mode though which is worrying.  That shouldn't be happening and I am not sure how to diagnose the problem.

"add the null space as fixed effects"  - basically just chop off the zeroes of the penalty matrix, construct the relevant covariates for the null space (e.g. thin plate in two dimensions it would just be adding x and y coordinates as fixed effects), then only doing the laplace approximation integrating out the non-null-space parameters.  I haven't tried this yet.

Has anyone else had any experience with this stuff?  I'd be interested in discussing this if so.

I am particularly interested in low-rank approximate smoothers (like thin plate, duchon splines etc) because my model has a lot of parameters and I run out of memory if I use something like b-splines (too many random effects params to track and the model falls over at the optimising tape stage).

Andy Seaton
PhD Candidate
Centre for Research into Ecological and Environmental Modelling
University of St Andrews

Hi Andrew

Once I tried to incorporate a Thin Plate Spline (2D in the plane) as a random effect in TMB but I did not get good results. However, that was only because I did not have a complete understanding with c++. I'm working in my thesis in a low rank approximation for radial basis functions (aka kernel methods) and I'm happy to see someone with similar questions.

Andy

> > > > If the penalty matrix has a null space then some of the columns are zero and GMRF()will throw an error.  There are various approaches to dealing with this, I have tried two of them and I am considering a third.  I'll summarise them:

matrix: http://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/classUNSTRUCTURED__CORR__t.html

1s on the diagonal and the elements of theta filled in, row-wise, as the
lower-triangular elements).  We then compute D=diag(L L'), d = D^{-1/2},
and C = d L L' d.

  My question: is there a known/straightforward way/has anyone written
code to *invert* this transformation, i.e. compute theta given (the
lower triangle of) C?  I've only gotten as far as directly computing D =
(1, 1+theta_0^2, 1 + theta_1^2 +theta_2^2, 1 + theta_3^2 + theta_4^2 +
theta_5^2, ...) and trying to figure out if there's something useful I
can do with it ...

   I could do it by brute force (i.e. use optim() to minimize the sum of
squared deviations between (lower tri(C)) and (lower tri(US(theta))),
where US is the transformation specified above, but I feel like there
must be a better solution ...?
